h1: The 5 Best 4K Video Switchers for Live Streaming of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five 4K video switchers for live streaming, scored on inputs, SDI and HDMI mix, ISO recording, PTZ control and streaming.
summary: The Osee GoStream Duet 8 ISO is our top pick: four 4K HDMI and four SDI inputs, clean per-camera recording and direct RTMP streaming. The FoMaKo KC800 is the best PTZ-focused alternative, the Tenveo suits Ethernet-heavy setups, the FoMaKo KC602 is the leaner 4K60 option, and the unbranded dual-input unit is the budget entry.
intro: A 4K label on a video switcher tells you almost nothing about what the box does with 4K. Some accept 4K inputs and output only 1080p, some pass 4K through but mix at lower resolution, and some are 4K from end to end. For a live stream that most viewers watch at 1080p, the more important questions are how many cameras you can cut between, and whether you can record each one cleanly.

We ranked five 4K switchers by what their listings commit to: input count and types, recording features, PTZ camera control and direct streaming. Most pages are dense with slogans and short on numbers, so we report only the figures stated, and we mark where the output resolution is not 4K.

products.name: Osee GoStream Duet 8 ISO Live Streaming Video Switcher
products.verdict: Four 4K HDMI and four SDI inputs, ISO recording and direct RTMP streaming in one box.
products.description:
The Duet 8 ISO features four 4K HDMI and four SDI physical inputs, records clean individual feeds from all inputs, and supports direct hardware RTMP streaming to major platforms.

It leads because ISO recording is what separates a streaming mixer from a production tool: each camera is saved separately, so you can re-edit the show afterward without the on-air cuts. Eight inputs in a mixed HDMI and SDI layout also lets one box serve a camera crew and a laptop, which the four-input models cannot.

Buy it for a multi-camera church, sports or event stream. It is in the $500+ band, so it is overkill for a solo streamer with two cameras.

keySpecs.label: Recording
keySpecs.value: Clean ISO feeds from all inputs

products.idealFor: Multi-camera event, church and sports streams.
products.skipIf: You run one or two cameras on a modest budget.

products.name: FoMaKo KC800 4K 60FPS HDMI Multi-Cam Streaming Video Mixer Switcher
products.verdict: A hybrid switcher and PTZ controller with 24-bit RGB color processing.
products.description:
The KC800 is billed as a hybrid video switcher and PTZ controller with extensive interfaces for pro workflows and RGB 24-bit true color technology, handling 4K at 60 frames per second.

It ranks second because merging camera control into the switcher cuts a separate joystick controller from your setup, a real saving for churches and classrooms with pan-tilt-zoom cameras. It trails the Duet 8 on documented recording features and on a stated input count.

Buy it if your cameras are PTZ and you want one desk to cut and aim them. The listing does not state a clean-ISO recording feature, so confirm what it can record before assuming it matches the Osee.
products.idealFor: PTZ camera setups where one desk should do everything.

products.name: Tenveo 4K60FPS HDMI Video Switcher Mixer
products.verdict: A 4K HDMI plus SDI mixer with dual-channel streaming over Ethernet.
products.description:
Tenveo describes a professional 4K HDMI plus SDI video mixer switcher at 4K 60 frames per second, with dual-channel streaming via Ethernet.

It ranks third because dual-channel streaming means you can send to two destinations at once, say a platform and a backup, over wired Ethernet rather than Wi-Fi. It matches the KC800 on frame rate but publishes less on camera control, and it lacks the Osee's stated ISO recording.

Buy it for a wired studio that streams to two places at once, such as a platform and a private archive server. No input count is given in the listing, so verify how many HDMI and SDI ports you actually get, and whether the SDI is input or output only.
products.idealFor: Wired studios streaming to two destinations.
products.skipIf: You rely on Wi-Fi or need ISO recording.

products.name: FoMaKo 4K HDMI Video Mixer Switcher
products.verdict: The KC602: 4K60 input, 4K loop-through output and PTZ presets.
products.description:
This FoMaKo listing identifies the KC602, which takes 4K60 input and offers a 4K loop-through output, extensive input and output interfaces, and multi-camera PTZ control with intelligent presets.

It ranks fourth because it shares the KC800's PTZ strengths in a plainer package, and the 4K loop-through output lets you feed a confidence monitor or recorder at full resolution. It documents less than the Osee on recording and streaming.

Buy it for a smaller PTZ rig that wants preset recall for sermons, classes or panel talks. The same product name appears on other FoMaKo listings, so confirm the KC602 model in the live title before ordering, and check how many camera inputs it carries.
cons: Easy to confuse with other FoMaKo listings
products.idealFor: Small PTZ rigs that need preset recall.
products.skipIf: You want stated ISO recording or direct RTMP.

products.name: Video Switcher for Live Streaming
products.verdict: Dual 4K60 inputs with 1080p output, low latency, for $50 to $100.
products.description:
This unbranded switcher lists dual 4K60 input with 1080p output, audio-video integrated capture, and speed transmission with ultra-low latency.

It ranks last because the output is 1080p, so the 4K claim describes input only, and two inputs limit it to simple cuts. For a solo streamer that is exactly the use case, and at $50 to $100 it costs a fraction of the other four.

Buy it for a two-camera or camera-plus-laptop setup streaming at 1080p. Do not expect 4K output, and look for support and firmware details before relying on it for paid events, because a nameless unit leaves you alone when something fails mid-show.
products.skipIf: You need 4K output or more than two inputs.

whatMatters.detail: Inputs are the sources you can cut between, and the type decides cable reach. HDMI suits short runs, while SDI locks and carries over long cables. The Duet 8 offers four of each. Count your cameras, add a laptop for slides, and leave one spare, then check the listing for exact port numbers.

A switcher may accept 4K sources yet output only 1080p, which is fine for most streams. The unbranded unit takes dual 4K60 input and outputs 1080p, while the KC602 offers a 4K loop-through. Check the output line, and decide whether a 4K record or monitor feed matters to you, since most platforms deliver 1080p and a 4K master mostly helps archived footage.

ISO recording saves each camera as its own file in addition to the mixed program. It lets you rebuild or fix the show in editing. The Duet 8 states clean individual feeds from all inputs. If you want to repurpose footage afterward, check that the listing states this, since it is rarely implied.

PTZ cameras pan, tilt and zoom remotely. A switcher with control built in, like the KC800 and KC602, lets you recall presets from the same desk. This removes a separate joystick. Check which control protocols the listing names, and confirm your cameras use one of them, because a camera that speaks a different protocol will not respond to presets from the desk.

Direct hardware streaming means the switcher sends the show without a computer. The Duet 8 supports RTMP, and the Tenveo adds dual-channel streaming over Ethernet. Prefer wired Ethernet for reliability, check which platforms are supported, and keep a computer-based backup running if the stream is important, so a network drop does not end the show.

faq.a: Only for long cable runs or broadcast cameras. HDMI is fine within about a room, but SDI locks and travels farther. The Osee Duet 8 and Tenveo offer both, while the budget unit is HDMI-focused. Count your longest cable run before choosing.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with 4K switchers?
faq.a: Assuming 4K input means 4K output. The unbranded unit takes dual 4K60 and outputs 1080p. Check the output line, and remember most platforms deliver 1080p anyway, so 4K sources mainly help your own recordings and archive copies.

faq.q: Is the Osee worth it over the FoMaKo KC800?
faq.a: If you need clean ISO recording and many inputs, yes. The KC800 wins when PTZ control from one desk matters more. Both sit in the $500+ band, so decide by workflow, not price, and note that neither listing states a latency figure.

faq.q: How do I set up a switcher for streaming?
faq.a: Connect cameras to the inputs, a monitor to the output, and Ethernet to the network. On the Duet 8 ISO or Tenveo, enter your platform's RTMP details. Test with a private or unlisted stream before going live, and check the audio levels as well.

faq.q: How do I keep a switcher reliable?
faq.a: Use locking SDI where possible, secure HDMI cables with clips, and keep firmware current. Dual-channel streaming on the Tenveo gives a backup destination. Always rehearse the full show before an event, including a deliberate cable pull to see how you recover.

faq.q: Can I use these with PTZ cameras from other brands?
faq.a: Possibly, if they share a control protocol. The KC800 and KC602 list PTZ control, but the listing does not name protocols. Confirm compatibility with your camera maker before relying on presets.

finalTake: The Osee GoStream Duet 8 ISO is the 4K switcher to buy: eight mixed inputs, clean ISO recording and direct RTMP streaming. The FoMaKo KC800 is the pick if PTZ control from the same desk is the priority, and the Tenveo adds dual-channel Ethernet streaming. The KC602 is a leaner PTZ option, and the budget dual-input unit suits solo streamers who only need 1080p output.
